Now I'll view one reference from each of my top 4 candidates.

**Analysis:**

- **Test image**: Very close-up of corn ear kernels. Tan/golden kernels with dense white cottony fungal mycelium filling between/underneath kernels, with some pinkish-red discoloration on certain kernels.
- **Gibberella**: Darker, gray-black discoloration with some white mold — doesn't match as well.
- **Fusarium**: Scattered white/pink mold on yellow kernels — partial match but less dense mycelium.
- **Diplodia_Ear_Rot**: Shows tan kernels with white dense cottony mycelium filling between kernels, similar brownish discoloration — strong match.
- **Trichoderma**: Green mold — no match.

The dense white mycelium filling between tan-discolored kernels, along with the characteristic pinkish-brown kernel discoloration in the cross-sectional close-up, is most consistent with Diplodia Ear Rot.
